physicalNotes: Radius 0.09724345 Jupiter radii from Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract): 6,952.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 0.01352931 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2024): P 1.4344555 d
sources.shape: Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2024): a/R* 10.97; Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2024): inclination 89.3 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2024): transit mid-time 2460076.902501 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 4 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
